# MCPJam API

> Programmatic access to the MCP servers in your MCPJam projects — diagnostics, tool calls, prompt rendering, and asynchronous eval runs.

> [!WARNING]
>
> **The MCPJam API is in preview.** It works today and we use it ourselves, but
> it has not been generally announced and the surface may change — including in
> breaking ways — while we finish the design. Pin your integration to the
> behaviors documented on this page, build a [tolerant
> reader](#versioning--stability), and expect to revisit it. Feedback is very
> welcome on [Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z) or
> [GitHub](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/issues).

> [card] [Create an API key](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)
>
> Go straight to key management in the hosted app. If you're signed out,
> you'll be asked to sign in and then land right back on the API keys page.

The MCPJam API lets you operate the MCP servers saved in your
[hosted](https://docs.mcpjam.com/hosted/overview.md) projects — from CI, scripts, or your own agents —
without opening the UI.

What you can do with it today:

* **Discover your resources** — list your projects, their servers, eval
  suites, and chat sessions, so every ID the other routes need is
  self-serve
* **Validate a server** — connect, initialize, and capture a capability snapshot
* **Run the doctor** — the probe → connect → initialize → capabilities workflow
* **Check OAuth requirements** — does this server need an OAuth grant?
* **List tools, prompts, and resources** — the server's MCP primitives
* **Call a tool / render a prompt** — execute primitives and get the MCP result back verbatim
* **Read a resource** by URI
* **Export a full snapshot** — tools, resources, and prompts as one JSON document
* **Manage a project's clients** — list, read, **create** (from a built-in
  template like `claude`/`chatgpt`/`cursor`, or from a full config), edit,
  duplicate, and delete the named, reusable configurations that define how
  MCPJam connects to and talks to your MCP servers. Edits are compare-and-set:
  read the client, then send its `configId` back as `expectedConfigId` for a
  config change and its `name` back as `expectedName` for a rename — a rename
  does not rotate the config, so the config token cannot detect a concurrent
  one — and a concurrent edit is rejected rather than silently reverted
* **Manage a project's environments** — list, read, create, edit, archive, and
  restore the named execution bundles (host + optional server group + optional
  pinned skills and plugin versions) that eval suites and goals run against,
  and **preview** what one resolves to before launching it
* **List a project's studies** — name, access mode, attached servers, and
  share link — and **read one study's settings**: model, system prompt,
  tool-approval policy, and resolved servers
* **Author eval suites** — create a runnable suite (name, default model, servers, test cases) synchronously and get a `suiteId` back; no run is started and no credits are spent
* **Run eval suites asynchronously** — create a run from a saved suite, get a `202` + `runId`
  immediately, then poll status, per-iteration results (tool calls, token
  usage, latency), and full traces. Runs appear live in the hosted UI,
  tagged `source: "api"`
* **Manage a server's accounts** — complete OAuth yourself (e.g. the SDK's
  `runOAuthLogin`, or your CI's own sign-in) and upload the token to a named
  account; list, rename, choose the default, and delete accounts. Tokens are
  write-only: no route returns one
* **Run a headless agent turn** — send a message history, get back the
  assistant reply, the platform operations it invoked, references to any
  resources it created (eval suites), and token usage; the model is pinned
  server-side and billed to the project
* **Send feedback** — report a bug, a missing capability, or something
  confusing to the MCPJam team at the moment you hit it; the same endpoint the
  `send_feedback` MCP tool calls

All endpoints operate on servers you have already added to a project in the
hosted inspector. Managing API keys remains UI-only — see
[Not in the API yet](#not-in-the-api-yet).

## Base URL

```text theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1
```

The API is path-versioned. All routes on this page are relative to the base
URL above.

## Authentication

Every request needs an MCPJam API key in the `Authorization` header:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -X POST \
  "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/tools" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{}'
```

### Creating a key

1. Open [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys)
   in the hosted app (the card at the top of this page takes you there
   directly).
2. Click **Create API key**, name it, and pick the **organization** it will act in.
3. Copy the key (`sk_…`) immediately — **it is shown exactly once** and never
   stored by MCPJam in retrievable form.

Keys can be revoked from the same page at any time. Revocation takes effect
immediately.

### Scope

A key is bound to one MCPJam organization at creation and acts **as you,
inside that organization**. Per-request authorization still applies: a call
only succeeds if the key's owner can access that project and server. A key
can never reach projects outside its organization.

> [!NOTE]
>
> Two deliberate restrictions while in preview:
>
> * **API keys cannot manage API keys.** Requests to the key-management surface
>   with an `sk_…` bearer fail with `403 FORBIDDEN`. Create and revoke keys in
>   the UI.
> * **Guest sessions cannot use the API.** Sign in to create keys.

### Keep keys secret

Treat an API key like a password:

* Load it from an environment variable or secret manager — never commit it to
  source control or ship it in client-side code.
* Scope keys narrowly: one key per integration, named so you can tell them apart.
* Rotate by creating a replacement key, switching traffic, then revoking the old one.
* If a key leaks, revoke it immediately in
  [**Settings → API keys**](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

If you see `401 UNAUTHORIZED` with `details.reason: "ORPHANED_KEY"`, the key
is no longer bound to an organization and cannot be used — create a new key
from [Settings](https://app.mcpjam.com/settings/api-keys).

## Conventions

**Requests.** Operations on servers are `POST` with a JSON body (most accept
an empty `{}`). **Reads** — the catalog listings and eval-run polling — are
`GET` and take their options (`cursor`, `limit`, filters) as query
parameters.

**Responses.** Three envelope shapes, used consistently:

| Kind | Shape |
| - | - |
| Single resource | The resource object directly |
| Collection | `{ "items": [...], "nextCursor": "..." }` — `nextCursor` omitted on the last page |
| Error | `{ "code": "...", "message": "...", "details": {...} }` with a matching HTTP status |

**Pagination.** Collections are cursor-based. Pass the previous response's
`nextCursor` as `cursor` in the next request (body field on `POST` lists,
query parameter on `GET` lists). Cursors are opaque — don't parse them.

**Authoring vs running suites.** `POST /eval-suites` creates a runnable suite
(the suite plus its test cases) **synchronously** and responds `201` with the
`suiteId`, WITHOUT running anything — author once, run later. `POST /eval-runs`
is the async counterpart: it validates and creates a run synchronously, then
detaches execution and responds `202` with a `runId`. Poll
`GET /eval-runs/{runId}` until `status` is `completed`, `failed`,
`cancelled`, or `timed_out`.

**IDs.** Every identifier the API takes is discoverable through the API
itself: `GET /projects` lists your projects, `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers`
lists each project's servers, and `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites`
lists its eval suites. Start from `GET /me` to confirm which account a key
acts as.

## Errors

Errors always use the canonical body `{ code, message, details? }`. The `code`
is stable and machine-readable; `message` is human-readable and may change;
`details` is an optional, unstructured bag.

| Code | HTTP | Meaning |
| - | - | - |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Missing, invalid, revoked, or orphaned key |
| `OAUTH_REQUIRED` | 401 | The **target MCP server** needs an OAuth grant — distinct from a bad key |
| `AUTH_REQUIRED` | 403 | The **target MCP server** allowed the connection and asked for sign-in on this call. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge. Your key is fine — see [Sign-in challenges](#sign-in-challenges) |
| `FORBIDDEN` | 403 | Key is valid but not allowed to do this — or the **target MCP server** rejected the credentials MCPJam presented (retrying with a different MCPJam key will not help; reconnect or re-authorize the server) |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 400 | Malformed body or parameters |
| `NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Unknown project, server, or resource |
| `CONFLICT` | 409 | The resource isn't in a state that accepts this write — a stale `expectedRevision`, a duplicate name, or an environment that can't currently be launched. Re-read and retry |
| `FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED` | 422 | The target server doesn't support this MCP capability |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | 429 | Too many requests — see [Rate limits](#rate-limits) |
| `SERVER_UNREACHABLE` | 502 | Could not connect to the target MCP server |
| `TIMEOUT` | 504 | The target MCP server connected but didn't respond in time |
| `INTERNAL_ERROR` | 500 | Something failed on our side |

New error codes may be **added** over time; treat unknown codes as
non-retryable failures unless the HTTP status says otherwise.

### Sign-in challenges

Some MCP servers allow the connection and ask for sign-in only on a protected
call. The API never starts a sign-in. It reports the challenge instead:

* **HTTP 401 from the MCP server** on `tools/call`: the API answers
  `403 AUTH_REQUIRED`. `details.authChallenge` carries the parsed challenge:
  its `source` (`http_401`), and the `error`, `requiredScope`, and
  `resourceMetadataUrl` the server sent, when present.
* **An `isError` result carrying `_meta["mcp/www_authenticate"]`** (the
  ChatGPT convention): the call succeeds, and the `CallToolResult` is returned
  unchanged with an additive `authChallenge` field (`source:
  "tool_result_meta"`). A field the server already set under that name is never
  overwritten.

`AUTH_REQUIRED` is not `UNAUTHORIZED`: your MCPJam key is fine, so a different
key will not help. Complete the OAuth flow for that server yourself, upload the
token to one of its [accounts](#server-accounts), and call again. See
[Mid-session sign-in](https://docs.mcpjam.com/inspector/lazy-authentication.md).

## Rate limits

Each key gets **60 requests per minute** sustained, with bursts up to **10**.
Exceeding it returns `429 RATE_LIMITED` with a `Retry-After` header (in
seconds):

```http theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 7

{ "code": "RATE_LIMITED", "message": "API key rate limit exceeded. Slow down and retry." }
```

Honor `Retry-After`, add jittered exponential backoff, and expect these limits
to be tuned during the preview.

Other `429`s — the per-minute brakes and daily budgets described with the
endpoints below — carry `Retry-After` whenever the refusal knows when it
lifts, which is the ordinary case. Treat it as a hint that is usually there
rather than a guarantee: a refusal that reaches you without one still needs
your backoff, so **never** block waiting for a header that may not come.

## Endpoints

Each endpoint is fully documented — request and response schemas, examples,
and an interactive playground — under **Endpoints** in the sidebar.

| `GET /projects` | Projects the key can access (optionally `?organizationId=`) |

| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}` | One revision: every tool's definition and the server info it reported. Fields listed in `droppedFields` were too large to store, so they are unknown, not absent |
| `GET /projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/revisions/{revisionNumber}/diff` | What changed since the revision before, or since `?from=`: tools added, removed and changed, and server info changes with both values. | `GET /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites` | The project's eval suites, with latest-run summaries |
| `GET`, `POST /projects/{projectId}/clients` | List clients, or create one from a template or full config |

**Project environments** — the named execution bundles (one host, optionally a
standalone server group, optionally pinned skills and plugin versions) that eval
suites and goals run against. Reads need project membership; **every write
needs project admin**. Writes are revisioned: pass the `revision` you last read
back as `expectedRevision`, and a stale value returns `CONFLICT` (409) instead
of overwriting a concurrent edit.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET`, `POST /projects/{projectId}/environments` | List environments (`?includeArchived=true` to include archived ones), or create one |
| `GET`, `PATCH /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}` | Read one environment, or edit it (send `null` to clear `serverAttachmentId`, `skillSelection`, or `pluginVersionIds`) |

| `POST /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/archive` | Archive it — reversible, and frees the name for a new one |
| `POST /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/restore` | Restore an archived environment |

row is kept and restore has real semantics: it re-checks the name and drops

reusable synthetic character; a **goal** is the task you point one at; a

under it. Nothing here starts anything — launching is

| - | - |
| `GET .../personas` | List the project's personas |
| `POST .../personas` | Create a persona (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |
| `GET .../personas/{personaId}` | One persona |
| `PATCH .../personas/{personaId}` | Update a persona. Goals reference it by id, so renaming is safe |
| `DELETE .../personas/{personaId}` | Delete a persona. **409** while goals still reference it |
| `GET .../goals` | List the project's goals |
| `POST .../goals` | Create a goal (accepts `Idempotency-Key`). `personaId` and `swarmId` must be in this project |
| `GET .../goals/{goalId}` | One goal |
| `PATCH .../goals/{goalId}` | Update a goal. `null` CLEARS `environmentIds`; `iterations` and `maxTurns` must be sent together |
| `DELETE .../goals/{goalId}` | **Archive** a goal — existing runs keep pointing at the definition they executed |
| `GET .../swarms` | List swarm containers |
| `POST .../swarms` | Create a swarm container (accepts `Idempotency-Key`) |
| `GET .../swarms/{swarmId}` | One swarm |
| `PATCH .../swarms/{swarmId}` | Update the container's defaults. Not a cascade — existing goals keep their own values |
| `DELETE .../swarms/{swarmId}` | **Archive** a swarm. The goals under it stay launchable |

candidates and **persist nothing**: feed what you want to keep to the create
routes above. That is also why neither accepts an `Idempotency-Key` — a call
with no effect has nothing to de-duplicate, and offering one would imply the
drafts are stable across retries when they are not.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST .../personas/generate` | Draft a slate of personas (and goals for each) grounded in a server attachment or an environment |
| `POST .../goals/generate` | Draft goals for a persona passed **by value**, so you can draft before you save |

> [!WARNING]
>
> The generation routes consume **no customer credits** — the model cost is on
> MCPJam. They are still subject to usage limits, and each limit means a
> different wait: a per-minute burst brake (`429`, retry in seconds), your
> organization's daily generation quota (`429`, resets at UTC midnight), and
> MCPJam's own daily budget for the feature (`429` with
> `details.code: "platform_capacity"`, resets at UTC midnight). All three carry
> `Retry-After` — honor it rather than guessing. `details.canTopUp` is `false`
> on every one: buying credits does not lift them, so do not retry in a loop
> or switch identities to get around them.

**Swarms — runs** (`/projects/{projectId}/goals/{goalId}/runs`,
`.../goal-runs/...`) — launching a goal and reading what it produced:

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals/{goalId}/runs` | That goal's runs, newest first |
| `POST .../goals/{goalId}/runs` | **Launch.** Answers `202` — the fan-out has started, not finished. Send `Idempotency-Key`. Optional `expectedSponsored` is how many conversations you expect MCPJam to sponsor; a different actual split is a `409` (`details.code: swarm_funding_changed`) and nothing is created. The response can report `funding` (`sponsored`, `credits`, `total`) |
| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}` | The full run: counts, per-target breakdown, per-session `attempts` |
| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/sessions` | The chat sessions the run produced (summaries, not transcripts) |
| `POST .../goal-runs/{runId}/cancel` | Stop a run. Idempotent — a second cancel is `200` with `alreadyCanceled: true`, not a `409` |

Three things worth knowing before you write the client:

* **Always send `Idempotency-Key` on a launch.** It spends model credits, so a
  retry of a dropped response must not run the goal twice. Replaying a key
  returns the original run with `deduped: true` and starts no second runner —
  and consumes no quota. Omitting the header is read as a request that declined
  to identify itself, and gets a fresh run every time.
* **Check `canceled` before reporting a failure.** A stopped run carries
  `status: "failed"`, because cancellation is recorded as a marker rather than
  a status of its own. `stale: true` is the third case: the runner went silent
  and the watchdog settled the run.
* **`targetId`, not `hostId`, identifies a target.** Two environments can
  resolve to the same host with different servers, so a run can hold two
  targets that share a `hostId`.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Launching **spends**: a run fans out into `targets × iterations`
> sessions. Two different `429`s can come back — the per-minute burst brake
> (retry in seconds) and your plan's daily launch cap (resets at UTC midnight).
> Both normally carry `Retry-After`; back off on your own when one does not.

**Swarms — insights** — what a run revealed. Read these in order of cost: the
roll-up and the scorecard are deterministic and free, the findings registry
aggregates them, and swarm run insights run a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../goals-overview` | Project roll-up: recent runs, goal-completion rates, repeat failures, trend |
| `GET .../goal-runs/{runId}/scorecard` | One run's deterministic rubric result. No model, no spend |
| `GET .../goal-findings` | Criteria that keep failing, tracked across swarm runs |
| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Hide a finding |
| `POST .../goal-findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Un-hide it |
| `GET .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Poll a swarm run's generated insights. **404 = nobody asked** |
| `POST .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Request them. `202` — scheduled, not done |
| `DELETE .../swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` | Cancel a generation still `pending` |

Two arithmetic traps worth naming, because both produce numbers that look
plausible and are wrong:

* **Divide by `sessionsGraded`, never by the session total.** Three failures
  out of four graded sessions, in a run that attempted forty, is 75% — not
  7.5%.
* **`failedGradingCount` is not `failCount`.** A crashed judge is not a
  regression, and folding the two together makes one look like the other.

And one modelling note: a finding's `status` is a lifecycle —
`new | recurring | regressed | resolved`. `dismissed` is *not* one of them.
Dismissal is the orthogonal `dismissedAt`, so a finding can be both recurring
and dismissed, and hiding one never claims it stopped happening.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting swarm run insights consumes **no credits** — the model cost is on
> MCPJam. It still counts against the `insightsPerDay` ledger, which counts
> REQUESTS and is **shared** with eval-run and user-testing insights, so a
> request here takes one from there too. Poll the `GET` rather than
> re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice.
>
> Three refusals, three different meanings: a short `429` is the per-minute
> brake (wait seconds), a `429` naming `insightsPerDay` is the daily ledger
> (its `Retry-After`, when present, counts to UTC midnight), and a `403` means
> the feature is not available to your organization — waiting will never help.

they did, and controlling who can reach it. A **study** is a published
environment: one per environment, addressed by its own id once it exists.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `PUT .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Publish.** Idempotent — republishing returns the existing study, and `created: false` says so. Project **admin** |
| `DELETE .../environments/{environmentId}/study` | **Unpublish.** The link dies and live sessions end. `deleted: false` when there was nothing published |
| `PATCH .../studies/{studyId}` | Rename, re-describe, or change `mode` |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions` | What visitors did: one row per session, with feedback and a first-message preview |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/sessions/{sessionId}` | One session's transcript, paged. Tool payloads and blobs are dropped |
| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/guest-execution` | The spend dial for anonymous visitors: daily credits, computer starts, concurrency |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rotate-link` | **Mint a new share link.** No body — the new secret is minted server-side |
| `PUT .../studies/{studyId}/members` | Invite someone (or change their role) on an `invited_only` study |
| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/members/{memberIdOrEmail}` | Remove someone. Their grant is revoked, ending their live sessions |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/rebind` | Point the study at a different environment in the same project |

> [!WARNING]
>
> **Rotating the link does not evict anyone who already used it.** It stops the
> old URL from granting NEW access; the grants already redeemed under it stay
> valid. That is the single most important thing to know here, because rotation
> is what you reach for when a link leaks — and on its own it does not undo the
> leak. Rotate *and* remove the members you did not intend to have.
>
> What DOES take effect at once, ending live sessions rather than waiting for
> expiry: unpublishing, tightening `mode`, and removing a member. Those bump
> the study's `accessVersion`, and a session minted under an older version
> stops working. None of them reverse by calling the opposite — a re-invited
> member gets a new session, not their old one.
>
> Read `accessVersion` off the publish and rebind responses. The update and
> rotate responses do not carry it.

**User testing — what visitors did** — the analytics reads, and the model pass
over them. Read these in cost order: metrics, usage and signals are
deterministic and free; the insights request runs a model.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/metrics` | Volumes, completion and feedback rates. `?population=real\|synthetic` splits real visitors from swarm runs |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/usage` | Which models, tools and servers the sessions used. **Check `scan.truncated`** before quoting a rate |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/signals` | What the miner found in the current window — and where you get the `windowId` |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/findings` | Every finding raised over this study, dismissed ones included |
| `GET .../studies/{studyId}/windows/{windowId}/insights` | One window's insights. **`404` means nobody asked**, which is not the same as `pending` |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | **No credits; counts against `insightsPerDay`.** `202` with the `windowId` to poll. `409` if the window has not been mined yet |
| `DELETE .../studies/{studyId}/insights` | Release a generation stuck `pending`. Takes `windowId` in the body |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/dismiss` | Dismiss a finding. Keyed on its stable id, so it stays dismissed when insights regenerate |
| `POST .../studies/{studyId}/findings/{findingId}/undismiss` | Undo that |

The `usage` response includes an `analysis` summary: `total`, `analyzed`,
`pending`, `running`, `failed`, `skipped`, and `deferred` describe session
coverage. Failure/skip reasons and `deferredUntil` explain incomplete work;
`awaitingTaxonomy`, `unassigned`, and `staleAssignments` distinguish catalog
coverage from extraction. `projectionPending` and `projectionFailed` describe
the map independently. Reading this response never starts analysis.

Taxonomy entries carry the published version and discovery status. Theme ids
remain stable across additions and cosmetic renames. An older assignment
version can still be valid when its theme is unchanged; a retired or replaced
membership remains visible while cached reassignment completes. These are
current views with version provenance, not historical traffic snapshots.

Check `scan.truncated` and `analysis.sampled` before interpreting coverage as a
whole-scope total. Map reads separately expose displayed counts, scope totals,
sampling, and freshness; a swarm run's displayed counts cover only its requested
goal runs. A pending projection contributes to the unmapped count rather
than a fabricated map node.

The five analytics shapes above are documented as **open objects** on purpose.
Their upstream projections grow with the product and the SDK types them the
same way, so pinning a field list would turn every new metric into a spec
violation. Read what you recognize; ignore the rest.

> [!WARNING]
>
> Requesting insights consumes **no credits** — the model cost is on MCPJam.
> It still draws on the same `insightsPerDay` ledger as eval-run and swarm run
> insights — one REQUEST quota, three producers. Poll the window read rather
> than re-requesting; `force: true` deliberately takes a second slice, which is
> why it is never inferred from anything else.

| Endpoint | What it does |
| - | - |
| `POST /feedback` | Send a bug report, missing-capability note, or other feedback to the MCPJam team. Body: `{ kind, summary, details?, operation?, requestId?, errorCode?, projectId? }`. Responds `201 { id, receivedAt, duplicate }` once stored. Signed-in accounts only (guests get `401`). Rate-limited per user (`429` with `Retry-After`). >
> `POST /feedback` is the same endpoint the `send_feedback` MCP tool calls.
> Include the failing call's `x-request-id` as `requestId` when you have one —

## Server accounts

A saved server signs in with one or more **accounts**. When your test users
can't use the browser sign-in, for example because a password and a passkey
are required every day, your CI can sign in itself and upload the fresh token
to a named account before each run.

| Endpoint (`/projects/{projectId}/servers/{serverId}/...`) | What it does |
| - | - |
| `GET .../accounts` | The accounts you can see: your own personal ones, or the project accounts of a server shared with the project |
| `GET .../accounts/{account}` | One account |
| `PUT .../accounts/{account}` | Upload a token. Creates the account (`201`) or replaces its token in place (`200`, same id) |
| `PATCH .../accounts/{account}` | Rename it (`name`), make it the default (`isDefault: true`), or both |
| `DELETE .../accounts/{account}` | Delete it, and ask the token's issuer to revoke the token |

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -fsS -X PUT \
  "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "tokens": { "sensitive_value": "[REDACTED]"$ACCESS_TOKEN"'", "expires_in": 3600 },
    "clientInformation": { "clientId": "'"$CLIENT_ID"'" }
  }'
```

Every answer is the account: its `id`, `name`, `kind`, `isDefault`,
`needsReconnect`, `hostedOnly`, `expiresAt`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`. No
route returns a token, and none can.

### Addressing an account

`{account}` is an account id or a name. A well-formed account id is always
read as an id: it matches that account or answers `404`, and an upload to an
unknown id never creates one. Anything else is a name, matched ignoring case.
A name no account has makes `PUT` create the account; on every other route it
answers `404`. A name two accounts share answers `409` with both ids in
`details.accountIds`.

A name is letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-`, starts with a letter or digit, and
is at most 64 characters. One outside that rule, or one that is also a
well-formed account id, is refused with `400`, never cleaned up. Names are
unique on the server, ignoring case.

### What an upload stores

* **Nothing checks who a token belongs to.** A name is your own label, and
  replacing a token replaces it whoever the token belongs to. Keep each name
  for one test user.
* **Uploaded accounts are hosted-only.** Hosted runs use them, and no local
  app, browser or sandbox ever receives their token, the account's owner
  included. Asking for it is refused with a message naming the rule.
* **The token is bound to the server URL saved in the project.** The body
  takes only `tokens` and `clientInformation`. A URL field (`serverUrl`,
  `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`) or `tokens.id_token` is
  refused with `400`, as is any field the route doesn't know.
* **Each token field is at most 16 KB.**
* **A refresh token is optional, and usually best left out.** When CI uploads
  a fresh token before each run, or when the issuer rejects our refreshes, a
  stored refresh token only adds a long-lived credential. Without one, an
  expired account lists `needsReconnect: true` and keeps its id until the next
  upload restores it.
* **Uploads are budgeted** per person and server: 60, refilling at 120 an
  hour. Past it the answer is `429` with `Retry-After`.

### Who can upload

An API key acts as the person who created it, with all of that person's
access. For personal accounts, upload with the key of a dedicated member who
is not a project admin, so a leaked CI key can't do an admin's work. On a
server shared with the project, accounts are project accounts: only a project
admin can upload, rename or delete them, and every member's hosted runs can
use them.

### Running evals as an account

A run with no saved account choice acts as the server's **default** account.
To run evals from CI as one account, upload its token, make it the default,
then start the run:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
curl -fsS -X PATCH \
  "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/servers/$SERVER_ID/accounts/test-automation-1" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "isDefault": true }'
```

The CLI takes the same steps with `mcpjam cloud server-accounts set`, which
reads the token from a file, an environment variable or stdin, and
`mcpjam cloud server-accounts default`. See the
[CLI reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/reference.md#cloud-server-accounts-commands).

The default is shared by every run that key starts, so don't run the same
key's runs at the same time with different defaults. Where your organization
has account choice for eval suites, a suite can instead save the accounts it
runs as, in its settings in the app; a run with a saved choice uses those
accounts and ignores the default.

### Deleting an account

`DELETE` removes the account and its stored token, and asks the token's issuer
to revoke the token where the issuer supports revocation. That is best effort,
and it also ends any copy of the same token you still hold. The default
account can't be deleted while other accounts exist (`409`): make another
account the default first.

### The deprecated import route

`POST .../oauth/import-tokens` still works, and is removed 90 days after the
accounts API shipped. It uploads to your default account, creating an unnamed
one when the server has none, and keeps its old body and its old
`{ imported, expiresAt }` answer. Every answer carries `Deprecation: true`, a
`Sunset` date and a `Link` to `.../accounts`.

An account this route creates is hosted-only. An existing default it writes
into keeps whatever rule it had. Its `serverUrl` must be the URL saved in the
project, or the answer is `400`. `authorizationServerUrl`, `oauthResourceUrl`
and `tokens.id_token` are accepted and ignored. Move to
`PUT .../accounts/{account}`, which names the account it writes.

The error codes these routes add to `details.code` are listed in the
[error code reference](https://docs.mcpjam.com/troubleshooting/error-codes.md#server-account-errors).

## Run evals from the API

The shortest useful loop — create a run with one inline test, then poll:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
# 1. Create (responds 202 immediately; -f + jq -e fail fast on errors)
RUN_ID=$(curl -fsS -X POST \
  "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "suiteName": "smoke",
    "serverIds": ["'$SERVER_ID'"],
    "tests": [{
      "title": "echo works",
      "runs": 1,
      "model": "anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5",
      "provider": "anthropic",
      "steps": [
        { "id": "s1", "kind": "prompt", "prompt": "Use the echo tool to say hi" },
        {
          "id": "s2",
          "kind": "assert",
          "assertion": {
            "type": "toolCalledWith",
            "toolName": "echo",
            "args": { "args": { "text": "hi" } }
          }
        }
      ]
    }]
  }' | jq -er .runId)

# 2. Poll until status is completed | failed | cancelled | timed_out
curl -s "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY"

# 3. If it did not pass, read the decision summary FIRST
curl -s "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/decision-summary" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY"

# 4. Or go straight to per-iteration tool calls, token usage, latency
curl -s "https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/eval-runs/$RUN_ID/iterations" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $MCPJAM_API_KEY"
```

The decision summary composes steps 2 and 4 into one versioned object so every
client reads a run the same way. Four things to know before gating on it:

* **`measurementUnit` ships with every count.** Under per-case grading the
  counts are case-execution *variants*, with iterations as trials inside them;
  under a suite-wide accuracy threshold they are trials. The same suite reports
  a different total under each — 3 against 15 for three cases run five times —
  so a count without its unit is not a fact, and a rate is never converted
  across that line.
* **It explains the verdict; it never re-decides it.** The run's own decision is
  the authority and is carried through on `decision`. The per-trial
  `diagnostics` sit underneath it — a case can pass with a failing trial in it,
  so tallying diagnostics gives a different answer than the platform reached.
* **`verdict: "notEstablished"` is not a failure and not `inconclusive`.** It
  means no verdict exists at all (unfinished, stopped early, or undecidable);
  `undecided.reason` says which. `inconclusive` *is* a decision — the validity
  phase ran and withheld a verdict.
* **`diagnostics.complete` says whether you have the whole list.** A page
  fetched with a `cursor` is never complete, and `scannedIterations` separates
  "nothing failed" from "we did not look".

Evidence is scoped to the claim it supports: for a measured failure the span
ids, prompt indexes and reasons come from the first failed stage's row alone,
and `evidence.tracePath` is an API-relative path you can append to your base URL
to read the full trace.

`model` takes an id from the hosted catalog — `provider/name` form, e.g.
`anthropic/claude-haiku-4.5` — and runs on your organization's credits.
Provider-native ids (e.g. `claude-sonnet-4-5`) are bring-your-own-key: pass
the key in `modelApiKeys`. A model the API can't execute is rejected at
create time with `VALIDATION_ERROR`; `details.hostedModels` lists the valid
hosted ids for that provider.

Reruns are even shorter: `{ "suiteId": "..." }` reruns the suite exactly as
configured, connecting the suite's saved server selection (the `202` response
lists the resolved `servers`). Pass `serverIds` to override the selection; a
suite with no saved selection requires it (`VALIDATION_ERROR` with
`details.reason: "NO_SAVED_SERVER_SELECTION"` otherwise).

### Running against a project environment

A [project environment](#endpoints) is launchable only through a suite that has
it **attached**. Attach them first with
`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}` and an `environmentIds`
array (send `null` to detach them all; `[]` is rejected — use `null`), then
pass `environmentId` on the run. It must be one of that suite's attached
environments; anything else is a `400` with
`details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_NOT_ATTACHED"`, raised before any case is
authored or any server connected.

Omitting `environmentId` is meaningful, and depends on the suite:

* **no** attached environments → the run uses the saved server selection, as before;
* **exactly one** attached → that environment is used automatically. The `202`
  response's `environment` field says so;
* **several** attached → `400` with `details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_REQUIRED"`,
  naming the candidates.

The environment supplies the closed server set — including the servers its
pinned plugin versions contribute — so `serverIds` is not required and is
**rejected** alongside it (`400`), rather than accepted and ignored: honoring
both would connect a different set than the run is stamped with. The same goes
for a `serverIds` override on an environment-based suite
(`details.reason: "ENVIRONMENT_SERVERS_NOT_OVERRIDABLE"`).

The run is pinned to the environment revision resolved at launch: if the
environment changes in between, the run is rejected with `CONFLICT` (409)
rather than executing against a different configuration than the one whose
tools were captured. Use
`GET /projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/resolve` to see what it
will connect before launching.

When creating a new inline suite, `POST .../eval-runs` also accepts `hosts: [{ host: "Claude", servers: ["my-server"] }]`, using the same host name or ID and optional server selection as `POST .../eval-suites`. A single host is selected for the run automatically. With multiple attachments, use `namedHostId` to select the run's client. For an existing suite, update its attachments first. If `hosts` is omitted, the backend supplies the project's default client.

Run reads and listings expose `client: { id, name, source, hostStyle?, modelId? }` when recorded. `id` is the named host ID or `null`; `source` is `environment`, `attached_host`, `suite_default`, or `sdk`. The name is durable even if the host is deleted. SDK executions use `SDK harness`; `launcher.client` separately identifies the launching process. Older runs without a descriptor omit `client`. `modelSource: "case"` means the run's sole model came from its case snapshot; `client_default` and `override` retain their existing meanings.

Every run records which environment it used. `GET .../eval-runs/{runId}` (and
the run listings) return `environment: { id, name, revision }` — read from the
run's immutable snapshot, not the suite's current attachments — or `null` for a
run that used a saved server selection.

Per-organization
concurrency is capped (default **2** concurrent runs); exceeding it returns
`429` with `details.reason: "CONCURRENT_RUN_LIMIT"` — wait for an active run
to finish.

If a server answers `401 OAUTH_REQUIRED`, complete the OAuth flow yourself
(the SDK's `runOAuthLogin` handles interactive, headless, and
client-credentials flows) and upload the token to one of the server's
[accounts](#server-accounts). Subsequent runs inject the stored token, and
refresh it server-side when you stored a refresh token.

## Reasoning effort

A reasoning effort is a **saved setting on a model selection**, not a free-standing
field. A `ModelSelection` (`modelId`, `source`, an optional `connectionRef`, and a
`fallback`) carries it as `settings.reasoningEffort`, and the same shape is
accepted everywhere a model choice is saved:

| Where | Field |
| - | - |
| Client (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/clients/{client}`) | `set.modelSelection` (or `config.modelSelection` on a whole-config replacement) |
| Project environment (`POST`, `PATCH`, `POST .../ensure-adhoc`) | `modelSelection`, read back on the environment |
| Eval case (`POST`, `PATCH .../cases`) | `models[].selection`, read back on the case |
| Eval suite (`PATCH /projects/{projectId}/eval-suites/{suiteId}`) | `executionConfig.modelSelection`, read back on the suite |

```json theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
{
  "modelId": "openai/gpt-5",
  "source": "hosted",
  "settings": { "reasoningEffort": "high" },
  "fallback": { "provider": "none", "model": "none" }
}
```

* **Levels.** `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`, `max`. Which of
  them a model accepts is `supportedReasoningEfforts` on each row of the public
  `GET /v1/models` catalog. An empty or absent list means no effort is offered for
  that model — do not guess one.
* **Applied or refused, never dropped.** A saved effort is applied by the route
  the run takes and recorded on the execution record, or refused with
  `capability_missing` before any spend. An effort replaces the sampling
  temperature.
* **A selection belongs to one model.** It must be for the `model` / `modelId` it
  sits beside (`400` otherwise); sent alone it pins its own model. A bare model
  change on a suite or environment drops a selection saved for the old model
  instead of failing.
* **Cases keep their selections.** A `models` PATCH replaces the array, but an
  entry that omits `selection` keeps the case's existing selection for that
  model. Send `selection: null` to drop it.
* **Clearing.** `null` clears a saved selection on a client `set`, an environment
  or a suite, keeping the bare model id.
* **Never a secret.** A selection has no credential field; an unknown key
  (`apiKey`, …) is a `400`.
* **Environments need the capability.** `GET .../environments/capabilities`
  reports `modelSelections`; an older deployment rejects the field.
* **`advancedConfig.reasoningEffort` is retired.** It was never applied, so
  writing it is a `400` pointing at `models[].selection.settings`, and a stored
  value is refused by the runner.

`POST /chat-sessions/messages` takes a top-level `reasoningEffort` for a
per-request effort. Like `temperature`, it is pinned on the session's **first
turn** (a continuation that restates it is refused), it wins over the effort a
`hostId`'s saved selection carries, and it cannot be combined with `temperature`.

The SDK, CLI, MCP tools and in-app agent all go through the same operations:
`--effort` / `reasoningEffort` is a shorthand that edits the selection the target
already has, and is refused (`send modelSelection`) when there is none.

## Versioning & stability

* The API is **path-versioned** (`/api/v1`). When it reaches general
  availability, breaking changes will require a new version path.
* **During the preview**, breaking changes to v1 may still happen; we'll note
  them in the [changelog](https://docs.mcpjam.com/changelog/overview.md).
* **Additive changes** — new endpoints, new optional request fields, new
  response fields, new error codes — are considered non-breaking and can ship
  at any time. Write clients that ignore unknown fields.
* Error **codes** are stable identifiers; error **messages** are not.

### Renamed surfaces

Three nouns this API used are now what the product calls them: `scenario` is
**study**, `journey` is **goal**, and `wave` is **swarm run**. The paths, the
operation names, the SDK types and the noun-bearing response fields all moved:

| Was | Is |
| - | - |
| `/projects/{projectId}/scenarios[/{scenarioId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies[/{studyId}]` |
| `/projects/{projectId}/user-testing/scenarios/{scenarioId}/…` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies/{studyId}/…` |
| `/projects/{projectId}/environments/{environmentId}/scenario` | `.../environments/{environmentId}/study` |
| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys[/{journeyId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/goals[/{goalId}]` |
| `/projects/{projectId}/journey-runs/{runId}` | `/projects/{projectId}/goal-runs/{runId}` |
| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys-overview`, `.../journey-findings` | `.../goals-overview`, `.../goal-findings` |
| `/projects/{projectId}/waves/{waveId}/insights` | `/projects/{projectId}/swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` |

Response fields followed their nouns: `scenarioId` → `studyId`, `journeyId` →
`goalId`, `waveId` → `swarmRunId`, and `sessionsPerTarget` → `iterations`.

Two reads became one: `get_scenario` served the execution settings and
`get_user_testing_scenario` served the environment id and the insights
envelope. `get_study` returns both, and the two caller-dependent fields are
absent rather than null when you may not have them.

**Every old path still works** and is unchanged, including its old response
spellings. Each one answers with `Deprecation: true` and a `Link` header naming
its successor. They are undocumented on purpose — the spec is what a new
integration reads — and they are removed at general availability.

A handful of operations kept their names through the rename and so have no
deprecated twin to hold the old field spellings. `get_swarms_overview`,
`create_swarm` and `update_swarm` emit both and accept either — never both in
one request — until general availability.

### Vocabulary

A name can move behind an alias; a VALUE cannot. `sourceType` is one field with
one string in it, and a client switching on `"scenario"` has no second name to
fall back to. So the values negotiate.

Send `x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary: 2` and the renamed values read canonically:

| Field | Vocabulary 1 | Vocabulary 2 |
| - | - | - |
| session `sourceType` | `scenario` | `study` |
| session `parentRef.kind` | `scenario`, `journeyRun` | `study`, `goalRun` |
| session `parentRef` ids | `scenarioId`, `journeyRunId`, `journeyRefId` | `studyId`, `goalRunId`, `goalRefId` |
| share `resourceType` (field AND path segment) | `scenario` | `study` |
| trace-destination `sourceTypes` | `scenario` | `study` |

Absent means `1`, which is byte-for-byte today's contract. Any other value is a
`400`. On the way IN, a vocabulary-2 request may name a filter or a path segment
by either spelling; a vocabulary-1 request may use only the legacy one, because
a boundary that accepts a spelling it does not announce is one two
implementations can disagree about. A response that varies by vocabulary sends
`Vary: x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary`.

This is a **separate header** from `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary`, which is
eval-scoped by name and moves on its own schedule. A deployment may speak one
and not the other, so read
`GET /projects/{projectId}/capabilities` — `apiVocabulary` and `vocabulary` are
two blocks — before sending either. With the SDK:
`new PlatformApiClient({ …, apiVocabulary: 2 })`, or
`client.withApiVocabulary(2)` on one you already hold.

Permalink resource types are the exception that proves the rule: `study` and
`goal_run` are the canonical keys, `user_testing_scenario` and `journey_run`
still resolve to the same routes, and which one a response carries follows the
OPERATION rather than the header — a renamed operation derives the canonical
key, its deprecated twin the old one. `capabilities.apiVocabulary.resourceTypes`
lists both.

### Browser tools on chat sessions

> [!NOTE]
>
> Hosted browser availability depends on the account and deployment. The browser workspace must be enabled to open the live pane in the Playground.

`POST /chat-sessions/messages` accepts an optional `browser: { policy?, profileId? }`. Attach it on every turn that should browse. The initial grant and profile are fixed; the current host policy and pinned read-only mode can narrow the effective permissions. Responses and traces include the read-only `chatSessionId`, browser metadata, and screenshot URLs without inline image data.

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| - | - | - |
| POST | `/chat-sessions/browser` | Create an empty API session and its browser with `projectId`, `policy`, optional `profileId`, and a stable `idempotencyKey`. |
| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/open` | Open or wake the session browser. |
| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/command` | Execute a browser command under the session policy with a stable `commandId`. |

# CLI Overview

> Local MCP testing and mcpjam cloud: probing, debugging, OAuth, conformance, and hosted evals from your terminal

The `mcpjam` CLI is two invocations. Local MCP testing stays at the top level: inspect, debug, and test MCP servers from the command line or CI (connectivity, OAuth, MCP Apps, tools/resources/prompts, protocol conformance). Most local commands are one-shot; `mcpjam mcp` and `subscriptions listen` keep a process open. Account-bound commands live under `mcpjam cloud` and talk to your MCPJam account. ## Cloud credentials and API URL

`--api-key` and `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud` and work before or after descendants (`mcpjam cloud --api-key sk_… eval list` and `mcpjam cloud eval list --api-key sk_…` are the same). Local commands, including hosted `readiness`, reject those flags at the program root. Hosted `readiness` still takes leaf `--api-key`.

Credential precedence for Cloud commands:

1. `--api-key` — must be an `sk_` key. A `mcpjam_…` legacy key is a usage error.
2. `MCPJAM_API_KEY` — same `sk_` rule. A legacy value in this env var is ignored (with a warning) so SDK eval reporting can still use it.
3. Stored OAuth from `mcpjam cloud login`
4. Missing — Cloud commands fail with login guidance before they hit the network (`mcpjam cloud status` reports `missing` instead)

API URL precedence:

1. `--api-url`
2. `MCPJAM_API_URL`, or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` (the same server without `/api/v1`)
3. The server saved with the OAuth login (only when that login is the credential; a login saved before logins recorded their server counts as MCPJam Cloud, and one whose recorded server is not a usable address is refused with exit `3`)
4. `https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1`

Every command that can contact MCPJam (it accepts `--api-url`, or it uploads results) decides its server when it starts, before it contacts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` that is not an `http(s)` URL, or that carries credentials, a query or a fragment, is a usage error (exit `2`), and so are the two variables naming different servers. The error masks credentials, a query and a fragment, and does not repeat a value that is not a URL. A saved login is only sent to its own server: when it is the credential and the order picks another server, the command exits `3` before any request. `mcpjam cloud status` uses the same checks but stays network-free: it still emits the complete JSON report, sets `ok: false`, includes `credential.valid` / `deployment.valid` plus an `error` string, and exits `1`. Missing credentials are informational (`credential.valid: null`) and successful.

Successful Cloud commands print an audience line to stderr (`Using MCPJam Cloud as … · project: … · <apiUrl>`). `--quiet` suppresses it. Machine-readable JSON stays on stdout. `cloud status` redacts API keys.

## Cloud project scope

Most Cloud commands pick one project:

1. `--project <id-or-name>`
2. An explicit `project` field in `--file` / `--json`
3. `MCPJAM_PROJECT`
4. The nearest valid `.mcpjam/project.json`
5. Automatic — the most recently updated project you can see

Empty `--project` or `MCPJAM_PROJECT` is a usage error. `MCPJAM_PROJECT_ID` does **not** select a Cloud CLI project (it is SDK eval reporting only).

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam cloud login
mcpjam cloud link                  # writes .mcpjam/project.json (no secrets)
mcpjam cloud status                # zero-network: credential, deployment, selector
mcpjam cloud eval list             # uses the link
mcpjam cloud link --remove
```

`mcpjam cloud eval` run-inspection commands (`status`, `cancel`, `judge`, `iterations`, `gate`, `compare`, `trace`, `steps`, `screenshot`, `video`) follow the same rule — `--project` is optional. `mcpjam cloud sessions list` does too; `--all-projects` restores a cross-project listing and cannot be combined with `--project`. ## What `--host` means

`--host` is not one flag. The meaning depends on the command:

| Where | What it selects |
| - | - |
| `server`, `tools`, `resources`, `prompts` | An **AI client** (`claude`, `chatgpt`, `cursor`, …). The CLI sends that host's `clientInfo`, capabilities, and protocol version in `initialize`. |
| `test --host` | One host **template** to emulate for a local suite run: its handshake, tool visibility and model settings. Never the real client. |
| `compat --host` | Which AI clients to report. Repeatable; default is all. |

| `cloud environments --host-id` | The project Host id the environment runs as. Distinct from eval's `--host`. |

`--host` on a local command is mutually exclusive with `--client-capabilities`. A Cloud `--host` is mutually exclusive with `--server` / `--environment` when those already supply a closed server set.

## Global flags

These flags apply to every command. Cloud credentials `--api-key` / `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud`, not the program root.

| Flag | Default | Description |
| - | - | - |
| `--timeout <ms>` | `30000` | Request timeout in milliseconds |
| `--rpc` | off | Include raw JSON-RPC request/response logs in JSON output under `_rpcLogs` |
| `--quiet` | off | Suppress non-result progress output on stderr |
| `--no-telemetry` | off | Disable anonymous telemetry for this invocation |
| `--format <format>` | `human` on TTY, `json` when piped | Raw output format (`json` or `human`) |
| `-v, --version` | | Print the CLI version |

## Output formats

The CLI auto-detects whether stdout is a terminal:

* **Interactive terminal** — defaults to `--format human`. For most commands this is pretty-printed JSON; `server doctor` and the OAuth conformance commands provide dedicated human-readable summaries.
* **Piped or redirected** (CI, `| jq`, agent invocation) — defaults to `--format json`, the full structured result.
* **Conformance in CI** — `protocol conformance`, `protocol conformance-suite`, `oauth conformance`, `oauth conformance-suite`, `apps conformance`, and `apps conformance-suite` support `--reporter junit-xml` and `--reporter json-summary`.
* **Explicit `--format`** always wins over the auto-detected default.

**For agents**: raw JSON is the source of truth. Human format is a lossy presentation layer. If you're parsing output programmatically, pass `--quiet --format json`.

JSON-valued flags accept inline JSON, `@path`, or `-` for stdin. `tools call` also accepts `--tool-args-stdin` as a shorthand for `--tool-args -`. Use files or stdin for large payloads to avoid shell escaping issues:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
echo '{"key":"value"}' | mcpjam tools call --url $URL --access-token $TOKEN \
  --tool-name my_tool --tool-args - --quiet --format json
```

## Connecting to servers

The CLI supports two transport modes, selected by which flags you pass:

* `--url ...` selects HTTP.
* `--command ...` selects stdio.
* `--transport http|stdio` is optional and acts as an explicit override/validator when you want the CLI to reject mismatched flags early.

### HTTP (Streamable HTTP / SSE)

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp
```

Add auth when needed:

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
# Static bearer token
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --access-token $TOKEN

# OAuth tokens from a prior login
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --oauth-access-token $TOKEN

# Custom headers
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --header "X-API-Key: $KEY"
```

### Stdio (local subprocess)

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
mcpjam server doctor --command node --args server.js --cwd /path/to/project -e API_KEY=[REDACTED]
```

Stdio child processes inherit the parent shell environment by default. Use
`-e/--env` to add values or override inherited ones for the spawned server.
Structured debug artifacts only record the explicit env keys you pass through
`-e/--env`; inherited shell variables are not enumerated.

> [!NOTE]
>
> `oauth ...` and `protocol ...` are HTTP-only command groups. They do
> not accept stdio targets.

## Update notifications

After a successful command, the CLI checks whether a newer version of `@mcpjam/cli` is available and prints a notice to stderr when one is found:

```
Update available: @mcpjam/cli 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0
Run npm install -g @mcpjam/cli to update
```

The check is non-blocking: version data is fetched in a detached background process and cached locally for 24 hours, so it never slows down your commands. The notice is written to stderr only and never touches stdout or JSON output, so it is safe for both interactive terminals and AI agents (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) that capture stderr. It is suppressed automatically in CI.

To opt out, set one of these environment variables before running any command:

| Variable | Effect |
| - | - |
| `MCPJAM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1` | Disable update checks for `@mcpjam/cli` |
| `NO_UPDATE_NOTIFIER=1` | Disable update checks (conventional npm opt-out) |
| `CI=true` | Automatically suppressed in CI environments |

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
| - | - |
| `0` | Success / all checks passed |
| `1` | Command ran but reported a failure (e.g., server unhealthy, conformance failed) |
| `2` | Invalid arguments or configuration |

## Quick triage workflow

The fastest path from "I have a server URL" to "I know what's wrong":

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
# 1. One-shot health check (probe + connect + sweep)
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp

# 2. If oauth_required: get a token
mcpjam oauth login --url https://your-server.com/mcp \
  --protocol-version 2025-11-25 --registration dcr

# 3. Re-run doctor with the token
mcpjam server doctor --url https://your-server.com/mcp --oauth-access-token $TOKEN

# 4. Exercise tools directly
mcpjam tools list --url https://your-server.com/mcp --access-token $TOKEN
mcpjam tools call --url https://your-server.com/mcp --access-token $TOKEN \
  --tool-name my_tool --tool-args @params.json --quiet --format json

# 5. If the server exposes MCP Apps, validate the ui:// surface
mcpjam apps conformance --url https://your-server.com/mcp --access-token $TOKEN

# 6. Render one UI-capable tool result in Inspector's App Builder.
# --ui opens Inspector by default in a TTY; add --no-open if browser automation already opened it.
mcpjam tools call --url https://your-server.com/mcp --access-token $TOKEN \
  --tool-name my_app_tool --tool-args @params.json --ui --quiet --format json
```

## Use from an MCP client instead of a shell

If your agent speaks MCP but can't run shell commands (Claude Desktop, chat clients), run the same testing engine as a stdio MCP server:


Connections to servers under test stay open between tool calls, so agents can also observe notifications and session behavior that one-shot CLI commands can't. See [MCPJam as an MCP server](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/mcp-server.md).
